walkthroughs.body_html:
Life in the Universe — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Life in the Universe brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Life in the Universe.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Solar wind

mcqs.q: What is the current best estimate for the age of the universe?
options: Galaxies only move in random directions.
About 6,000 years.
Infinite.
About 13.8 billion years.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It is the hottest stage.
Galaxies only move in random directions.
